## 1. Reproduce the data example

Use the saved LD and the same association simulation as `01-get-started` (seed 4).

```{r}
library(susieRobust)
ld <- readRDS("data/getting-started/ld.rds")
R <- ld$R; R0 <- ld$R0; N <- ld$settings$N
J <- ncol(R)
L_true <- 3L; L_max <- 10L; h2 <- 0.01

set.seed(4)
causal <- sort(sample.int(J, L_true))
beta <- numeric(J)
beta[causal] <- rnorm(L_true)
beta <- beta * sqrt(h2 / ((1-h2) * drop(crossprod(beta, R %*% beta))))
e <- eigen(R, symmetric=TRUE)
stopifnot(min(e$values) > -1e-8)
v <- drop(R %*% beta + e$vectors %*% (sqrt(pmax(e$values, 0)/N) * rnorm(J)))
```

## 2. Fit IW and double eta0

First estimate eta0, then hold it fixed at twice that estimate in a new fit.
Lambda remains free to be estimated in both fits.

```{r}
fit <- susie_iw(v=v, R0=R0, N=N, L=L_max, max_iter=1000, tol=1e-6)
eta0 <- fit$eta0
fit_2eta0 <- susie_iw(v=v, R0=R0, N=N, L=L_max, max_iter=1000, tol=1e-6,
                     eta0_fixed=2 * eta0)

data.frame(fit=c("IW", "IW: doubled eta0"),
           eta0=c(fit$eta0, fit_2eta0$eta0),
           lambda=c(fit$selected_lambda, fit_2eta0$selected_lambda),
           converged=c(fit$converged, fit_2eta0$converged))
```

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
plot_pip(fit, causal=causal, R=R0, main="IW: learned eta0")
plot_pip(fit_2eta0, causal=causal, R=R0, main="IW: fixed at 2 x eta0")
par(mfrow=c(1,1))
```


## 3. Intial eta_0

One thing that I do not really happy about the previous fit it that it has a saddle point in the ELBO, which may suggest an early stop if the tol is not set to small. Now let me try to intialize eta_0 to large value to see if we can avoid this behavior

```{r}
fit <- susie_iw(v=v, R0=R0, N=N, L=L_max, max_iter=1000, tol=1e-6, eta0_init = 3000)
plot(fit$elbo, type = "l")
```

```{r}
plot_pip(fit, causal=causal)
```

So it looks like initialize at a higher eta0 does help. The default is 1000.

## 4. IW without purity filtering

We can recover credible sets from the existing `fit` without fitting IW again.
Purity filtering is a reporting step: setting `min_abs_corr = 0` retains sets
regardless of their LD purity, while still calculating purity for inspection.
If SER fallback
was used, its top-level posterior is the fallback result, so we instead use the
saved original IW posterior. Neither `fit$sets` nor `fit$raw_sets` alone recovers
discarded sets, since both were constructed using the original purity threshold.

```{r}
iw_posterior <- fit
if (isTRUE(fit$postprocess$fallback_used)) {
  iw_posterior <- list(alpha = fit$raw_alpha,
                       V = fit$raw_fit$sigma2,
                       pip = fit$raw_pip)
}
cs_no_purity <- susieR::susie_get_cs(
  iw_posterior, Xcorr = fit$purity_R, coverage = 0.95,
  min_abs_corr = 0, n_purity = ncol(fit$purity_R)
)
cs_no_purity$purity
```

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
plot_pip(iw_posterior,
         sets = if (is.null(cs_no_purity$cs)) list() else cs_no_purity$cs,
         causal = causal, R = fit$purity_R,
         main = "IW: no purity filtering")
```

```{r}
fit$V

```

Some of the sets got filtered out because of being deduplicated. 

```{r}
cs_all <- susieR::susie_get_cs(
  iw_posterior, Xcorr = fit$purity_R,
  coverage = 0.95, min_abs_corr = 0,
  dedup = FALSE, n_purity = ncol(fit$purity_R)
)

length(cs_all$cs)
data.frame(
  component = names(cs_all$cs),
  size = lengths(cs_all$cs),
  duplicate = duplicated(cs_all$cs)
)
```
